text:
rio (PM): Quick sync on credit guardrails for next sprint. Need a simple default and enterprise overrides.

anya (Revenue): We should sell credits as the billing unit. Default monthly allotments by tier + volume discounts. Also a safety cap for low-tier to prevent surprise invoices.

kevin (Eng): Enforcement choices: soft-delay (add latency), hard-429, or downgrade to cheaper model. Prefer soft-delay then 429 to keep UX graceful.

maria (Sales): Field feedback: customers dislike 429s during demos. Recommend promo-code credits for demos and a console top-up button.

li (Legal): Top-ups ok if marked non-refundable and logged. Auto-topup must be opt-in in contract. Add abuse detection clause.

billing-bot: billing-bot: billing.events now supports promo_credit and manual_topup events.

rio (PM): Proposed defaults: Hobby=5k credits/mo, Pro=100k, Scale=1M. Emergency top-up SKU available in console. Throttle policy: 30s soft-delay window, then 429.

anya (Revenue): Pricing suggestion: $0.0006/credit with stepped discounts at 1M and 10M thresholds. Cap hobby spend to $50/mo.

kevin (Eng): We'll add response headers: X-Credits-Remaining, X-Soft-Window-Remaining. Clients can show warnings when remaining < 10%.

maria (Sales): I'll pick two pilot customers for demo promo codes. Need a one-pager for pilot terms.

li (Legal): I'll draft two short clauses: one for top-ups, one for auto-topup opt-in. Will share for review.

rio (PM): Launch checklist: API docs, console top-up UX, billing integration, legal snippets, pilot one-pager, and monitoring dashboards (credit_burn, caps_hit). Follow-up Friday 9am PT.

anya (Revenue): Also track refunds_requested and emergency_topup_count.

kevin (Eng): I'll deliver API spec and PR by Wednesday.

rio (PM): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
